assertion.name: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
assertion.description: Langerhans cell histiocytosis and metastatic neuroblastoma can both produce bone lesions of the orbit in children. LCH tends to involve the skull bones, especially the lateral orbital roof, and the orbit is a common site of neuroblastoma bone metastases. At imaging, osseous orbital lesions may appear similar to each other, and LCH, granulocytic sarcoma and neuroblastoma metastases to the orbit are often bilateral. The Euro Histio Net guideline for patients up to 18 years lists neuroblastoma among the possible other conditions in its differential-diagnosis table for LCH involving the orbit. The same table also lists neuroblastoma among the possible other conditions for LCH skin nodules, with mastocytosis, juvenile xanthogranuloma and infant leukemia.
distinguishing_features: LCH tends to involve the skull bones, especially the lateral orbital roof, and produces lytic bone destruction with a sclerotic rim and a large intraorbital soft-tissue mass, whereas neuroblastoma metastases to the orbit cause an aggressive periosteal reaction in the orbital roof or lateral wall.
A definitive diagnosis of LCH requires positive immunostaining of the lesional cells for CD1a and/or CD207 (langerin).

selected_evidence.snippet: Positive immunohistochemistry staining for CD1a and CD207 (langerin) are required for a definitive diagnosis.

assertion.name: Hepatoblastoma
assertion.description: A review of infantile hepatic hemangioma lists metastatic neuroblastoma, hepatoblastoma and mesenchymal hamartoma among the primary differential diagnoses of a focal liver lesion in an infant that may be a focal hemangioma, so both tumors are considered when an infant has a focal liver lesion. A pedunculated hepatoblastoma, attached to the liver by a vascular pedicle and presenting as a perihepatic mass, can also be taken for neuroblastoma: in one reported four-month-old infant, a hepatoblastoma in the left upper quadrant was first suspected to be neuroblastoma on abdominal ultrasound. That presentation rests on a single case and establishes a diagnostic pitfall rather than its frequency.
distinguishing_features: In the reported four-month-old, bone marrow aspiration and 24-hour urinary VMA and HVA were negative for neuroblastoma; with CT showing nutrient vessels entering the mass from the left hepatic vein, coarse calcification and its enhancement pattern, pedunculated hepatoblastoma was suggested, serum AFP was above 100,000 ng/ml (the report's normal range is 5-109), and percutaneous biopsy confirmed hepatoblastoma.

The case report's authors conclude that pedunculated hepatoblastoma should be considered when a perihepatic mass in a child can be confused with other upper abdominal masses such as an adrenal mass, and that the vascular pedicle should then be looked for on imaging and the AFP check kept in mind.

A 2006 management review states that histology is essential for differential diagnosis and may be omitted only in some hepatoblastoma patients of the typical age (6 months to 3 years) with an excessively elevated serum alpha-fetoprotein.

selected_evidence.snippet: Histological diagnosis is essential for differential diagnosis and may only be omitted in some hepatoblastoma patients of the typical age (6 months to 3 years) with an excessively elevated serum-alpha-fetoprotein.

assertion.name: CNS neuroblastoma, FOXR2-activated
assertion.description: Shares the word neuroblastoma but not the disease. CNS neuroblastoma, FOXR2-activated is an embryonal brain tumor, one of four entities that DNA methylation profiling separated from tumors diagnosed as CNS primitive neuroectodermal tumors, and it is characterized by structural rearrangements converging on FOXR2. Peripheral neuroblastoma arises in the adrenal gland or the sympathetic chain, so the site usually settles the question. The overlap that does matter is FOXR2 itself: about 9 per cent of peripheral neuroblastomas express it, where it marks a subset with unfavorable outcome rather than this entity.
distinguishing_features: An intracranial site rather than adrenal or paraspinal
Structural rearrangements converging on FOXR2 characterize the entity; FOXR2 expression alone does not identify it, since about 9% of peripheral neuroblastomas express it
A distinct DNA methylation class, the basis on which it was separated from other tumors diagnosed as CNS primitive neuroectodermal tumors

selected_evidence.snippet: Genome-wide sequencing revealed complex inter- and intrachromosomal re-arrangements converging on forkhead box R2 (FOXR2) in 6/8 samples with available data, leading to increased FOXR2 gene expression levels in CNS NB-FOXR2 tumors compared with other CNS tumor entities

assertion.name: Ewing sarcoma
assertion.description: In its section on clinical and radiological diagnosis, the GEIS clinical practice guideline lists metastatic neuroblastoma among the differential diagnoses of Ewing sarcoma, with osteomyelitis, osteosarcoma, lymphoma, leukemia and Langerhans cell histiocytosis. On tissue both are small round cell tumors, and Ewing sarcoma is a differential diagnosis of poorly differentiated neuroblastoma.
distinguishing_features: Nuclear PHOX2B staining favors neuroblastoma; in one immunohistochemistry study PHOX2B immunostaining was negative in every Ewing sarcoma tested, and its authors call PHOX2B specific for neuroblastoma in its differential diagnosis with other small round cell tumors. A second series found all 20 Ewing sarcomas among its comparison tumors negative, with positivity defined as nuclear staining in at least 5% of cells, and its authors conclude that PHOX2B reliably distinguishes neuroblastoma from mimics such as Ewing sarcoma. PHOX2B is not fully sensitive, though; that series found it in 70 of 76 peripheral neuroblastic tumors (68 of 72 pediatric cases), so a negative stain does not exclude a peripheral neuroblastic tumor.

CD99 immunonegativity is one of the features that help distinguish neuroblastoma from other small round cell tumors, and NKX2.2 is described as a marker of Ewing sarcoma, a differential of poorly differentiated neuroblastoma; one metastatic neuroblastoma has nonetheless been reported as immunoreactive for both on cytology of the metastatic site, and its authors stress evaluating the primary site because cytology has limits.

Ewing sarcoma cells show intense, diffuse membranous CD99 and nuclear NKX2.2 immunoreactivity, but the GEIS guideline notes that neither marker is entirely specific for Ewing sarcoma and that genetic confirmation is required for the diagnosis; every Ewing sarcoma harbors a FET-ETS fusion.

selected_evidence.snippet: Immunohistochemically, neoplastic cells show a membranous pattern of intense and diffuse CD99 expression (Fig. 1B) and NKX2.2 nuclear immunoreactivity (Fig. 1C). However, it is important to note that CD99 and NKX2.2 are not entirely specific for ES ... Genetic confirmation is required for ES diagnosis. ... All cases of ES harbor a FET-ETS fusion.

assertion.name: Townes-Brocks syndrome
assertion.description: Townes-Brocks syndrome combines thumb malformations with imperforate anus, dysplastic ears, and renal anomalies. That combination reproduces most of the non-hematologic FA presentation at once, and FA patients may present with a Townes-Brocks phenotype. The anal and renal findings also overlap the VACTERL features listed above, so both differentials are typically live together.
distinguishing_features: Townes-Brocks syndrome is autosomal dominant and caused by SALL1 variants; a dominant family history argues against FA.
Neither progressive marrow failure nor crosslinker hypersensitivity occurs in Townes-Brocks syndrome.

selected_evidence.snippet: FA patients may also present with a phenotype characteristic of Seckel syndrome, Nijmegen breakage syndrome, Dubowitz syndrome, Holt-Oram syndrome, thrombocytopenia absent radius (TAR) syndrome, Townes-Brocks syndrome

assertion.name: Holt-Oram syndrome
assertion.description: Holt-Oram syndrome is the classic heart-hand syndrome, with upper-limb radial-ray defects and congenital cardiac malformation. Both limb and cardiac findings occur in FA, and FA patients may present with a Holt-Oram phenotype. Like TAR and VACTERL this differential is live at birth, long before FA declares itself hematologically.
distinguishing_features: Holt-Oram syndrome is autosomal dominant and caused by TBX5 variants; a positive family history in a dominant pattern argues against FA.
Neither marrow failure nor crosslinker hypersensitivity occurs in Holt-Oram syndrome.

assertion.name: Thrombocytopenia-absent radius syndrome
assertion.description: TAR syndrome pairs bilateral radial aplasia with thrombocytopenia, so it reproduces both halves of the FA presentation that a clinician would otherwise treat as diagnostic. FA patients may present with a phenotype characteristic of TAR.
distinguishing_features: Thumbs are present in TAR syndrome despite absent radii; FA radial-ray defects typically involve the thumb.
Thrombocytopenia in TAR is present from infancy and tends to improve; FA marrow failure is progressive and pancytopenic.
Chromosomal breakage testing with DEB or MMC separates the two.

assertion.name: Dyskeratosis congenita
assertion.description: Dyskeratosis congenita is a telomere biology disorder presenting with progressive marrow failure, cancer predisposition, and mucocutaneous findings including abnormal skin pigmentation, so it overlaps FA on the pigmentary, hematologic, and oncologic axes at once.
distinguishing_features: The mucocutaneous triad of reticulated pigmentation, nail dystrophy, and oral leukoplakia favors dyskeratosis congenita.
Very short lymphocyte telomeres for age support dyskeratosis congenita.
Radial-ray limb defects are characteristic of FA and not of dyskeratosis congenita.

selected_evidence.snippet: These include physical anomalies, as well as single or multiple cytopenias, macrocytic red blood cells and elevated fetal hemoglobin levels.

assertion.name: Dubowitz syndrome
assertion.description: Dubowitz syndrome presents with growth restriction, microcephaly, a characteristic facies, and eczematous skin change. It overlaps FA on growth deficiency, microcephaly, and cutaneous findings, and FA patients may present with a Dubowitz phenotype. Reported cases have also included cytopenias and malignancy, which narrows the clinical gap further.
distinguishing_features: Radial-ray and thumb defects are characteristic of FA and are not a defining feature of Dubowitz syndrome.
Crosslinker-induced chromosomal breakage testing is the discriminator where the clinical picture is growth restriction with microcephaly and skin change.

assertion.name: Nijmegen breakage syndrome
assertion.description: Nijmegen breakage syndrome is a DNA double-strand break repair disorder with microcephaly, growth deficiency, chromosomal instability, and cancer predisposition. FA patients may present with a phenotype characteristic of Nijmegen breakage syndrome, and both disorders show chromosomal instability, so the differential turns on which clastogen the cells are sensitive to.
distinguishing_features: FA cells are hypersensitive specifically to DNA interstrand crosslinkers (DEB, MMC); Nijmegen breakage syndrome cells are radiosensitive.
Progressive bone marrow failure and radial-ray defects favor FA.
Marked combined immunodeficiency with recurrent sinopulmonary infection favors Nijmegen breakage syndrome.

assertion.name: Seckel syndrome
assertion.description: Seckel syndrome is a microcephalic primordial dwarfism with severe proportionate growth restriction and marked microcephaly. It overlaps FA on growth deficiency and microcephaly, and FA patients may present with a Seckel phenotype. The overlap is not only clinical: several Seckel genes act in the ATR-dependent DNA damage response, so both disorders sit in the broader genome-instability space.
distinguishing_features: Growth restriction in Seckel syndrome is prenatal in onset and far more severe than the short stature typical of FA.
Radial-ray defects and progressive marrow failure point to FA rather than Seckel syndrome.
Crosslinker-induced chromosomal breakage is the discriminator; Seckel cells are not characteristically crosslinker-hypersensitive.

assertion.name: Diamond-Blackfan anemia
assertion.description: Diamond-Blackfan anemia is an inherited bone marrow failure syndrome that shares FA's combination of congenital anomalies, including thumb malformations, with cytopenia, macrocytosis, and raised fetal hemoglobin. This differential becomes live at the hematologic presentation rather than the malformation one.
distinguishing_features: Chromosomal breakage testing separates FA from the non-FA inherited bone marrow failure syndromes as a group.
Diamond-Blackfan anemia is a selective erythroid aplasia; FA marrow failure is typically trilineage.
Elevated erythrocyte adenosine deaminase supports Diamond-Blackfan anemia.

assertion.name: Drug-associated oesophageal or oropharyngeal candidiasis
assertion.description: Iatrogenic candidiasis from inhaled or systemic corticosteroids, broad-spectrum antibiotics, chemotherapy or other immunosuppression - by far the commonest explanation for oesophageal or oropharyngeal candidiasis in general practice, and a reversible one.
distinguishing_features: Clear temporal relationship to the drug exposure, with resolution on withdrawal, dose reduction, or spacer and mouth-rinse technique correction
Absent childhood history of thrush, nail or genital candidiasis; no family history
Normal Th17 counts and no STAT1 phosphorylation abnormality

selected_evidence.snippet: Oesophageal candidiasis is a common, usually self-limiting opportunistic infection, but long-term infection with Candida is known to predispose to oral and oesophageal squamous cell cancer (SCC).

assertion.name: Autoimmune polyendocrine syndrome type 1 (APECED/APS-1)
assertion.description: The most consequential overlap. CMC is typically the FIRST manifestation of APS-1, appearing years before the endocrine features, so an apparently isolated CMC in a child may be a pre-endocrine APS-1. This is a temporal trap, not merely a phenotypic one: withholding the diagnosis risks a fatal unrecognized adrenal crisis. APS-1 is simultaneously an APECED subtype of CMC (modelled in has_subtypes) and a differential diagnosis for apparently isolated CMC - both framings are correct and both are recorded here deliberately.
distinguishing_features: Neutralizing anti-IL-17A/IL-17F/IL-22 autoantibodies are present in APS-1 and absent in STAT1 GOF CMC, making autoantibody testing the decisive discriminator
Hypoparathyroidism, primary adrenal insufficiency and ectodermal dystrophy
Biallelic AIRE variants
Because the autoantibodies precede the CMC, a negative endocrine screen at presentation does not exclude APS-1 and surveillance is required
assertion.notes: Full curation of APS-1 (AIRE, thymic tolerance failure, endocrine autoimmunity) is in kb/disorders/Autoimmune_Polyendocrine_Syndrome_Type_1.yaml and is intentionally not duplicated in this entry.

selected_evidence.snippet: None of the patients displays autoantibodies against IL-17A, IL-17F, and IL-22.

assertion.name: DOCK8 deficiency

disease_term.preferred_term: combined immunodeficiency due to DOCK8 deficiency

term.label: combined immunodeficiency due to DOCK8 deficiency

assertion.description: A combined immunodeficiency with reduced Th17 numbers, in which CMC occurs as one feature alongside a much broader infectious and atopic spectrum. Unlike the selective IL-17-circuit disorders, CMC here is a downstream symptom of broad T-cell dysfunction rather than the organizing lesion, so it is modelled as a differential diagnosis rather than a subtype of this entry.
distinguishing_features: Recurrent, severe herpes simplex virus, herpes zoster, molluscum contagiosum and human papillomavirus infections not seen in isolated IL-17-circuit CMC
Recurrent otitis media, sinusitis and pneumonia, plus atopy (eczema, food allergy, asthma) and eosinophilia
Biallelic DOCK8 loss of function on sequencing; combined T- and B-cell dysfunction on immune workup rather than the normal lymphocyte subsets seen in isolated CMC

selected_evidence.snippet: Autosomal recessive DOCK8 deficiency is associated with a novel variant of combined immunodeficiency.

assertion.name: HIV infection / AIDS
assertion.description: The commonest acquired cause of persistent oropharyngeal and oesophageal candidiasis, and the single most important diagnosis to exclude before invoking an inborn error. CD4 depletion removes the Th17 compartment among much else, so the mucosal phenotype can be indistinguishable at presentation.
distinguishing_features: Positive HIV serology or nucleic acid testing with CD4 lymphopenia
Adult or adolescent onset rather than infancy, with no childhood history of thrush, nail or genital candidiasis
Accompanied by the wider spectrum of opportunistic infection (Pneumocystis, CMV, cryptococcosis) that pure IL-17-circuit CMC never produces
No family history; HIV testing is a mandatory part of the CMC work-up

selected_evidence.snippet: Secondary immune deficiencies are most often due to human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection, antibiotic use and immunosuppressive treatment (steroids, chemotherapy).

assertion.name: RORC deficiency and Mendelian susceptibility to mycobacterial disease

disease_term.preferred_term: autosomal recessive Mendelian susceptibility to mycobacterial diseases due to complete RORgamma receptor deficiency

term.label: autosomal recessive mendelian susceptibility to mycobacterial diseases due to complete RORgamma receptor deficiency

assertion.description: Sits at the CMC/MSMD boundary. Patients present with both candidiasis and mycobacterial disease, and the mycobacterial susceptibility arises through a mechanism (defective Mycobacterium-specific IFN-gamma production) that is separate from, not a consequence of, the IL-17 defect.
distinguishing_features: Disseminated BCG or Mycobacterium tuberculosis disease alongside the candidiasis
Absent palpable axillary and cervical lymph nodes and small thymus
Absence of MAIT and type 1 NKT cells
Biallelic RORC loss-of-function; pure IL-17-circuit CMC carries no mycobacterial risk

selected_evidence.snippet: We studied seven patients from three unrelated consanguineous families with this unusual combination of infectious diseases but with no known genetic disorder.

assertion.name: Severe combined immunodeficiency and other combined immunodeficiencies
assertion.description: CMC is one of many infections in patients with broad and profound T-cell deficiency. Because thrush is often the first visible sign in infancy, SCID can be mistaken for isolated CMC at the earliest presentation.
distinguishing_features: Failure to thrive, chronic diarrhoea and a broad infectious spectrum (Pneumocystis, disseminated viral infection, BCG disease) rather than Candida alone
Profound T-cell lymphopenia and abnormal lymphocyte subsets; abnormal newborn TREC screening
In CMC proper, T, B and NK cell numbers are normal, so quantifying them is the standard first-line discriminator

selected_evidence.snippet: CMC is one of a multitude of infectious diseases observed in patients with broad and profound T cell deficiencies.

assertion.name: Diabetes mellitus
assertion.description: Poorly controlled diabetes is a common metabolic permissive state for recurrent oral, cutaneous and genital candidiasis, and is also part of the STAT1 GOF and APS-1 autoimmune spectra - so it can be either the explanation for the candidiasis or a clue to the underlying inborn error.
distinguishing_features: Hyperglycaemia and raised HbA1c, with resolution of candidiasis on glycaemic control
Adult onset without childhood thrush, nail or oesophageal disease
Conversely, type 1 diabetes arising in a child who already has CMC should raise suspicion of STAT1 GOF (4% of the international cohort) or APS-1 rather than being accepted as the cause

selected_evidence.snippet: Many patients had autoimmune manifestations (37%), including hypothyroidism (22%), type 1 diabetes (4%), blood cytopenia (4%), and systemic lupus erythematosus (2%).

assertion.name: Autosomal dominant hyper-IgE syndrome (Job syndrome)

disease_term.preferred_term: hyper-IgE recurrent infection syndrome 1, autosomal dominant

term.label: hyper-IgE recurrent infection syndrome 1, autosomal dominant

assertion.description: Shares the IL-17 deficit and therefore the CMC, but is a multisystem syndrome rather than a selective antifungal defect.
distinguishing_features: Markedly elevated serum IgE with eosinophilia
Recurrent cold staphylococcal skin abscesses and pneumonia with pneumatocele formation
Eczematoid dermatitis
Retained primary dentition, characteristic facies, scoliosis, minimal-trauma fracture and joint hyperextensibility
A dominant-negative STAT3 variant; none of these features accompany pure IL-17-circuit CMC

selected_evidence.snippet: patients with the autosomal dominant (AD) hyper IgE syndrome, caused by dominant-negative mutations of STAT3, are susceptible principally to CMC and staphylococcal diseases of the lungs and skin

assertion.name: Secondary (acquired) chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis, general
assertion.description: An umbrella differential covering acquired, non-germline permissive states for persistent mucocutaneous candidiasis - most often HIV infection, systemic or inhaled corticosteroids and other immunosuppression, broad-spectrum antibiotic use, poorly controlled diabetes mellitus, or thymoma with anti-cytokine autoantibodies - that must be excluded before an inborn error of the IL-17 circuit is diagnosed. The three most clinically important individual causes (HIV/ AIDS, drug-associated candidiasis, diabetes mellitus) are curated as their own differential-diagnosis entries above with cause-specific distinguishing features; this entry records the shared acquired-cause framing rather than duplicating that detail.
distinguishing_features: No family history and no childhood-onset thrush, nail or genital candidiasis preceding the acquired insult
Clear temporal relationship to the immunosuppressive drug, HIV seroconversion, uncontrolled hyperglycaemia, or thymoma diagnosis
Same downstream complications (oesophageal stricture, squamous cell carcinoma risk) as the germline forms, but resolving or attenuating once the acquired cause is treated or removed

selected_evidence.snippet: Secondary immune deficiencies are most often due to human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection, antibiotic use and immunosuppressive treatment (steroids, chemotherapy).

assertion.name: Intellectual Developmental Disorder, Autosomal Recessive 75 (PIDD1)
assertion.description: Biallelic PIDD1 variants cause a neurodevelopmental disorder whose defining feature is a cortical malformation: a typical anterior-predominant pachygyria closely resembling the neuroimaging pattern of CRADD-related disease (MRT34), its PIDDosome partner. A recognisable neuroimaging malformation is one of the explicit disqualifiers for the non-syndromic category, and MONDO's own label for the class names variant lissencephaly, so this belongs with the malformation-of-cortical-development entities rather than here - notwithstanding that earlier PIDD1 families had been described as apparently non-syndromic, which is presumably how MONDO:0030785 came to sit under MONDO:0019502.

disease_term.preferred_term: intellectual developmental disorder, autosomal recessive 75, with neuropsychiatric features and variant lissencephaly

term.label: intellectual developmental disorder, autosomal recessive 75, with neuropsychiatric features and variant lissencephaly

distinguishing_features: Anterior-predominant pachygyria on neuroimaging, a gross cortical malformation rather than the subtle connectivity change this class permits.
Grouped mechanistically with CRADD-related disease through the PIDD1/CRADD/caspase-2 PIDDosome rather than with the MRT-series themes.
The earlier apparently non-syndromic description was superseded once systematic neuroradiology was applied to a larger cohort.

Criterion (i) of notes item 13 - the pachygyria is obligate across all eleven reported subjects and is described as typical, unlike the non-obligate callosal finding that leaves MRT61 inside the class.

selected_evidence.snippet: in eleven subjects displaying intellectual disability, behaviorial and psychiatric features, and a typical anterior-predominant pachygyria, remarkably resembling the CRADD-related neuroimaging pattern.

assertion.name: Intellectual Developmental Disorder, Autosomal Recessive 81 (ASCC3)
assertion.description: Biallelic ASCC3 variants cause a neuromuscular syndrome rather than isolated cognitive impairment. ASCC3 is a DNA helicase subunit of the four-part ASC-1 transcriptional cointegrator complex whose siblings ASCC1 and TRIP4 cause spinal muscular atrophy with congenital bone fractures, and the reported phenotype spans severe developmental delay to muscle fatigue with a genotype-phenotype correlation. A neuromuscular disease family, not a member of a class defined by isolated intellectual disability; MONDO files MONDO:0958204 under MONDO:0019502 nonetheless.
distinguishing_features: Neuromuscular involvement is the defining feature, not an accessory one.
Complex-level allelism with the spinal muscular atrophy with congenital bone fractures genes ASCC1 and TRIP4.
Biallelic loss of function appears not to be compatible with life, unlike the loss-of-function mechanism typical of this class.
Criterion (i) of notes item 13 - the neuromuscular phenotype is shared by all reported individuals and is what the entity is named for.

selected_evidence.snippet: Here we report the discovery of ASCC3 as the cause of a neuromuscular syndrome in seven unreported individuals from six unrelated families and updates on the one previously reported family.

assertion.name: Al-Raqad Syndrome (DCPS)
assertion.description: A named recessive syndrome caused by biallelic DCPS variants, and a differential rather than a member of this class. DCPS is the scavenger decapping enzyme acting in the last step of the 3' to 5' mRNA decay pathway - the counterpart of EDC3 (MRT50), which is curated here as a subtype - so the two share a discovery report and a theme but not a category: the DCPS report describes a syndrome with craniofacial anomalies and neuromuscular defects alongside the intellectual disability, which is the constellation whose presence disqualifies a case from the non-syndromic label. MONDO nevertheless files MONDO:0014648 as a direct child of MONDO:0019502; this entry records the disagreement rather than importing the concept.
distinguishing_features: Craniofacial anomalies present, which the non-syndromic category excludes.
Neuromuscular involvement present, which the non-syndromic category excludes.
Named as a syndrome (Al-Raqad) in its own founding report - supporting context only, since notes item 13 makes obligate involvement rather than nomenclature the criterion.
Criterion (i) of notes item 13 - the craniofacial and neuromuscular involvement is present in every one of the three affected individuals reported, not in a subset.

selected_evidence.snippet: We have identified a DCPS pathogenic mutation in a large family with three affected individuals presenting with a novel recessive syndrome consisting of craniofacial anomalies, intellectual disability and neuromuscular defects.

assertion.name: Intellectual Developmental Disorder, Autosomal Recessive 80, with Variant Lissencephaly (CASP2)
assertion.description: Biallelic truncating CASP2 variants cause a neurodevelopmental disorder whose defining feature is a cortical malformation: a typical fronto-temporal lissencephaly with pachygyria that the report describes as remarkably resembling the CRADD and PIDD1 neuroimaging pattern. This is the same disqualifier, and the same PIDDosome, that places PIDD1 in this list rather than among the subtypes: CASP2 encodes caspase-2, the caspase the CRADD and PIDD1 complex activates, and this knowledge base already models that mechanism in its CRADD-Related Thin Lissencephaly entry, whose pathophysiology nodes are named for PIDDosome signalling and for reduced caspase-2-mediated developmental neuronal apoptosis. MONDO's own label for the class names variant lissencephaly. Declined on both criteria of notes item 13.

term.label: intellectual developmental disorder, autosomal recessive 80, with variant lissencephaly

distinguishing_features: Fronto-temporal lissencephaly with pachygyria on neuroimaging, a gross cortical malformation rather than the subtle connectivity change this class permits.

selected_evidence.snippet: All patients from whom brain MRIs were available had a typical fronto-temporal LIS and pachygyria, remarkably resembling the CRADD and PIDD1-related neuroimaging findings.

assertion.name: Syndromic Intellectual Disability
assertion.description: Any recognised syndrome in which intellectual disability is accompanied by a characteristic pattern of dysmorphic, malformative, metabolic, or neuroimaging features. The boundary is genuinely unstable in this class: several MRT-series genes (NSUN2, MAN1B1, ADAT3) have been reclassified as syndromic once larger series were phenotyped, and the class review notes that many ARID genes are pleiotropic with broad phenotypic spectra. A non-syndromic label assigned on a small cohort should be treated as provisional.
distinguishing_features: Presence of a consistent extra-neural gestalt on expert dysmorphology examination.
A recognisable neuroimaging malformation rather than subtle volume or connectivity change.
A diagnostic metabolic or biochemical abnormality.
Absence of all of these on adequate assessment defines the non-syndromic category, but adequacy of assessment scales with cohort size and follow-up duration.

selected_evidence.snippet: ADAT3-related intellectual disability is an important recognizable cause of intellectual disability in Arabia.

assertion.name: X-Linked Intellectual Disability
assertion.description: The historically better-characterised class of inherited non-syndromic intellectual disability, with more than 90 genes known well before the autosomal recessive class was opened up. In a family with affected males only, X-linkage and autosomal recessive inheritance can be indistinguishable on the pedigree, and fragile X remains a mandatory exclusion.
distinguishing_features: Male-only affectation with transmission through unaffected carrier females and absence of male-to-male transmission favours X-linkage.
Affected siblings of both sexes with consanguineous parents favours autosomal recessive inheritance.
Large consanguineous cohort studies still recover X-linked genes alongside autosomal recessive ones, so an assumption of autosomal recessive inheritance should not restrict variant filtering.
FMR1 repeat testing is a standard first-tier exclusion regardless of pedigree structure.

selected_evidence.snippet: More than 90 different gene defects have been identified for X-chromosome-linked intellectual disability alone, but research into the more frequent autosomal forms of intellectual disability is still in its infancy.

assertion.name: Autosomal Dominant Non-Syndromic Intellectual Disability
assertion.description: The sibling class and the principal differential in a simplex case. Both present as isolated intellectual disability without a syndromic gestalt, and the two cannot be distinguished clinically - only by the molecular result and the pedigree. Distinguishing them matters enormously for counselling: recurrence risk is 25% for recessive versus low (mosaicism-limited) for a de novo dominant lesion.
distinguishing_features: Dominant cases are typically simplex with a heterozygous de novo variant in a constraint-intolerant gene and no consanguinity.
Recessive cases are more often multiplex with affected siblings, homozygous variants inside a run of homozygosity, and frequently consanguineous parents.
Only trio or family-based molecular testing resolves the two; de novo dominant lesions also occur within consanguineous families, so a consanguineous pedigree does not settle the question.

selected_evidence.snippet: 50 genes already established in neurodevelopmental disorders (46 autosomal recessive, 2 X-linked, and 2 de novo)

assertion.name: Progressive or Degenerative Neurological Disease
assertion.description: Neurodegenerative and neurometabolic disorders can present in early childhood with apparent developmental delay before the progressive nature is evident. Because AR-NSID is a static developmental encephalopathy - a mis-built rather than a damaged circuit, with no degenerative, ischaemic, or inflammatory arm - loss of previously acquired skills is the single cleanest discriminator against this diagnosis.
distinguishing_features: Developmental regression (loss of acquired skills) effectively excludes AR-NSID.
Progressive neurological signs, evolving neuroimaging abnormality, or a deteriorating clinical course argue for a degenerative alternative.
In AR-NSID the gap versus peers widens with age because the developmental trajectory is shallower, not because skills are lost.

selected_evidence.snippet: Detailed physical and neurologic examinations in all study participants did not show microcephaly, organomegaly, phakomata, spasticity, weakness, neuropathy, visual deficits, feeding problems, or psychiatric disorders.

assertion.name: Allergic rhinitis
assertion.description: Allergic rhinitis is the commonest cause of recurrent paroxysmal sneezing and is the principal condition to exclude when sneezing attacks are reported. The overlap with PSR is limited to the sneeze itself: allergic sneezing follows IgE-mediated mast-cell mediator release after allergen re-exposure and is accompanied by nasal itch, watery rhinorrhoea, and congestion, whereas PSR is a brief burst locked to an abrupt light transition with no nasal inflammation. The two can coexist, and coexistence does not reclassify the photic trigger.
distinguishing_features: Trigger is allergen exposure (pollen, house dust mite, animal dander) rather than an abrupt light transition
Sneezing occurs together with nasal itching, watery discharge, and congestion rather than as an isolated short burst
Allergen-specific IgE or skin-prick sensitization can be demonstrated; PSR has no confirmatory test
Symptoms are sustained or seasonal rather than lasting seconds after a change in illumination
assertion.notes: Ontology caveat, stated here because this entry is the other half of the problem: MONDO asserts the idiopathic (vasomotor) non-allergic rhinitis differential below (`MONDO:0006004`) to be a *subclass of* this entry's `MONDO:0011786`. A consumer reasoning over the subclass hierarchy will therefore collapse the two differentials into one, despite the prose separating them on exactly the allergic/non-allergic axis. See the fuller caveat on that entry; the defect is upstream in MONDO, not a claim of either entry here.

assertion.name: Gustatory rhinitis
assertion.description: Gustatory rhinitis is a non-allergic rhinitis in which food ingestion provokes rhinorrhoea and sneezing. It sits between the rhinitides and the trigger-defined sneeze reflexes and is the nearest neighbour of snatiation: both are meal-associated, but gustatory rhinitis is driven by a property of the food rather than by gastric distension, and it produces prominent rhinorrhoea rather than an isolated sneeze burst. Hot and spicy foods are the classic and most frequently identified triggers, but the source study concluded that almost any food can be implicated, so an atypical food history does not exclude it. It appears to be common, so its co-occurrence with PSR is better treated as expected than as diagnostically meaningful.
distinguishing_features: Trigger is food ingestion - classically hot or spicy, most often chili peppers, though a wide range of foods is implicated - not a light transition
Rhinorrhoea is the dominant symptom rather than a short sneeze burst
Occurs during or shortly after eating, so it is separable from PSR on timing alone
Distinguished from snatiation by being driven by food properties rather than by stomach fullness
assertion.notes: No `disease_term` is attached because MONDO has no gustatory rhinitis term (checked with OAK against `sqlite:obo:mondo`). The available neighbours are unsuitable rather than merely imprecise: `MONDO:0003014` rhinitis is the shared parent of several entries here and so discriminates nothing, and `MONDO:0006004` vasomotor rhinitis names a different type of non-allergic rhinitis already used for a separate differential in this block, so attaching it would conflate two distinct entities (note that MONDO asserts that term *under* allergic rhinitis rather than as a non-allergic sibling - see the misclassification recorded on that entry). Following the same convention as the snatiation entry, no term is preferable to a wrong one; this is a second MONDO new-term-request candidate.

assertion.name: Idiopathic (vasomotor) non-allergic rhinitis
assertion.description: Non-allergic rhinitis produces sneezing and rhinorrhoea in response to non-immunological environmental triggers such as temperature change, strong odours, tobacco smoke, and air pollution, without demonstrable IgE sensitization. It is the closest phenocopy of PSR among the rhinitides because both are non-inflammatory and both are provoked by an abrupt environmental change; the discriminator is that the provoking change is thermal, chemical, or olfactory rather than photic, and that symptoms persist beyond the moment of exposure.
distinguishing_features: Triggered by temperature fluctuation, strong odours, tobacco smoke, or air pollution rather than by bright light
Chronic nasal congestion and rhinorrhoea accompany the sneezing; PSR is a self-limited sneeze burst
Allergy testing is negative, as it also is in PSR, so a negative test does not distinguish the two
assertion.notes: Because neither PSR nor idiopathic rhinitis has a confirmatory laboratory test, the separation rests on trigger specificity elicited by history. Ontology caveat: MONDO asserts `is_a: MONDO:0011786` (allergic rhinitis) for `MONDO:0006004`, placing this non-allergic entity under allergic rhinitis and inheriting hypersensitivity-reaction and allergic-respiratory-disease ancestry. This contradicts the very distinction the entry exists to draw, and a consumer reasoning over the subclass hierarchy would collapse this differential into the allergic rhinitis differential above it. It also contradicts MONDO's own logical definition of the term, whose `intersection_of` is rhinitis + regulation of vasoconstriction with no allergic component, and its NCIT-derived `def:` makes no mention of IgE. The term is nonetheless retained because it is the correct entity and the best available: the alternative is the undifferentiated `MONDO:0003014` parent. Treat the asserted parentage as an upstream defect to be reported to MONDO, not as a curation claim of this entry.

assertion.name: Sneezing secondary to lateral medullary syndrome
assertion.description: Lateral medullary (posterior inferior cerebellar artery) syndrome is a brainstem infarct involving the medulla, where the sneeze-execution circuitry resides, and sneezing has been described as a manifestation of it. Together with epilepsy it forms the only non-benign arm of this differential, and it is the reason a new-onset sneezing pattern in an adult should not simply be labelled a photic sneeze reflex.
distinguishing_features: Abrupt new onset in adulthood rather than a lifelong trait, and without a family history
Accompanied by the lateral medullary deficit pattern - crossed sensory loss, dysphagia, dysarthria, vertigo, Horner syndrome
Not reproducibly locked to an abrupt bright-light transition
Confirmed by neuroimaging (MRI) rather than by trigger history alone
assertion.notes: The medullary localization is what makes this differential mechanistically pointed: it lesions the same brainstem sneeze-execution circuit that the "General Sneeze Execution Circuit" pathophysiology node of this entry models as the shared final common pathway.

assertion.name: Trigeminal irritant-induced sneezing
assertion.description: Direct mechanical or chemical stimulation of the nasal mucosa (nasal hair plucking, pepper and other irritants, cold dry air, intranasal instrumentation) activates the trigeminal afferents of the ordinary sneeze reflex. This is the physiological reflex that PSR is presumed to borrow downstream, so the two share the final sneeze-execution circuit and differ only in the afferent stimulus. It should be excluded before a light transition is accepted as the trigger, because bright-light exposure often coincides with going outdoors, where cold air and airborne irritants are simultaneously encountered.
distinguishing_features: A direct nasal stimulus is identifiable (irritant, instrumentation, cold dry air) at the time of sneezing
Reproducible with the nasal stimulus in the absence of any change in illumination
Occurs in essentially everyone, whereas PSR is present in a susceptible minority

assertion.name: Snatiation (stomach-fullness sneeze reflex)
assertion.description: Snatiation is an involuntary sneeze burst provoked by gastric distension after a large meal. It is the closest nosological relative of PSR: both are benign, familial, trigger-specific sneeze reflexes reported to segregate in a dominant-like fashion in selected kindreds, and both are diagnosed purely on the reproducible trigger. The distinction is the eliciting stimulus, and the two traits can be reported in the same individual.
distinguishing_features: Trigger is a particularly full stomach after eating, not sudden bright light
Sneezing follows meals rather than light transitions, so a food diary or meal-linked history separates the two
No visual or ocular component and no relationship to illumination
assertion.notes: The trait was described as an autosomal dominant sneezing disorder provoked by fullness of the stomach (PMID:2769729) and later given the backronym SNATIATION (PMID:2325110); both are brief letters without abstracts, so no snippet-verified quote is available and the claim is carried here by the review citation. No `disease_term` is attached because MONDO has no current term for this trait: the only candidate, MONDO:0007645 "gastric sneezing" (xref OMIM:137130), is obsoleted, and per convention no term is preferable to a wrong or deprecated one. This is a candidate for a MONDO new-term request.

selected_evidence.snippet: Sneezing can further be triggered through sudden exposure to bright light, a particularly full stomach and physical stimulants of the trigeminal nerve, as a result of central nervous system pathologies such as epilepsy, posterior inferior cerebellar artery syndrome or as a symptom of psychogenic pathologies.

assertion.name: Jugulotympanic paraganglioma ("glomus jugulare" / "glomus tympanicum")
assertion.description: This is a NAMING COLLISION, not a biological differential. The skull-base and middle-ear tumours historically called "glomus jugulare" and "glomus tympanicum" are PARAGANGLIOMAS and are NOT glomus tumours in the sense of this entry. They arise from neural-crest-derived parasympathetic paraganglia of the jugular bulb and tympanic plexus, are neuroendocrine (chromogranin / synaptophysin positive, with S100/SOX10-positive sustentacular cells), are associated with germline SDHx variants, may be catecholamine-secreting, and are managed by skull-base surgery or stereotactic radiosurgery. They share nothing with the pericytic MIR143-NOTCH-driven soft-tissue glomus tumour except the nineteenth-century use of "glomus" for a vascular body. Anyone reaching this entry from a "glomus jugulare" query has the wrong entity: see MONDO:0021064 (jugulotympanic paraganglioma) instead.
distinguishing_features: Anatomic site is the jugular foramen / middle ear rather than the acral soft tissue or nail bed
Neuroendocrine chief-cell morphology with chromogranin and synaptophysin expression, and S100/SOX10-positive sustentacular cells; glomus tumour is S100-negative and actin-positive
Derived from neural-crest paraganglia, not from perivascular modified smooth muscle
Germline SDHx predisposition; no MIR143-NOTCH fusion
May secrete catecholamines and present with pulsatile tinnitus and lower cranial neuropathy, not with the paroxysmal-pain/cold-sensitivity triad
assertion.notes: Curation guardrail. This is the single most consequential entity-resolution error for this disease name, and it is exactly the Named Entity Confusion failure mode described in CLAUDE.md: literature retrieved for "glomus tumor" will silently include head-and-neck paraganglioma papers whose PMIDs are real and whose snippets validate. Check that any candidate reference is about an acral/soft-tissue lesion before citing it here.

selected_evidence.snippet: Jugulotympanic paragangliomas (JTPs) are rare, hypervascular skull base tumors.

assertion.name: GLI1-altered soft tissue tumour (GLI1-fused or GLI1-amplified)
assertion.description: The most contemporary addition to the pericytic/perivascular differential. A distinct group of soft tissue neoplasms defined either by GLI1 gene fusions (ACTB, MALAT1 or PTCH1 partners) or by GLI1 amplification with CDK4 and MDM2 co-amplification shows monomorphic ovoid-to-epithelioid cells in a nested-trabecular pattern separated by thin septa and a delicate capillary network. The authors of the defining series call this architecture highly reminiscent of glomus tumour and list glomus tumour/myopericytoma explicitly among the differential diagnoses. The distinction is prognostic, not academic: unlike conventional glomus tumour these are malignant soft tissue tumours, with high mitotic counts, necrosis, lymphovascular invasion and documented lymph node and lung metastases, and they cannot be separated from glomus tumour on morphology alone.
distinguishing_features: GLI1 gene fusion, or GLI1 amplification usually with CDK4 and MDM2 co-amplification, rather than a MIR143-NOTCH fusion
Frequent S100 positivity and an inconsistent immunoprofile (CD56, SMA, pan-CK variably positive); glomus tumour is consistently actin-positive and S100-negative
High mitotic count and necrosis in a substantial minority, with lymphovascular invasion
Malignant behaviour is the rule rather than the rare exception it is in glomus tumour
assertion.notes: MONDO has no class for GLI1-altered / GLI1-amplified soft tissue tumour (a MONDO search for "GLI1" returns only the HGNC gene record), so this differential is deliberately recorded without a disease_term rather than mapped to an approximate parent.

Sporadic solitary glomus tumour is a somatic, fusion-driven NEOPLASM; glomuvenous malformation is an inherited GLMN-related vascular MALFORMATION in which a somatic second hit (usually acquired uniparental isodisomy of 1p) unmasks the germline allele locally. They are not two presentations of one lesion, and evidence about one must not be transferred to the other.

Germline GLMN loss of function with a somatic second hit (paradominant), not a MIR143-NOTCH fusion
Dilated venous channels with only a few layers of glomus cells, rather than solid sheets of glomus cells

assertion.description: The most contemporary addition to the pericytic/perivascular differential. A distinct group of soft tissue neoplasms defined either by GLI1 gene fusions (ACTB, MALAT1 or PTCH1 partners) or by GLI1 amplification with CDK4 and MDM2 co-amplification shows monomorphic ovoid-to-epithelioid cells in a nested-trabecular pattern separated by thin septa and a delicate capillary network. The authors of the defining series call this architecture highly reminiscent of glomus tumour and list glomus tumour/myopericytoma explicitly among the differential diagnoses. The distinction is prognostic, not academic: unlike conventional glomus tumour these are malignant soft tissue tumours, with high mitotic counts, necrosis, lymphovascular invasion and documented lymph node and lung metastases, and they cannot be separated from glomus tumour on morphology alone.
distinguishing_features: GLI1 gene fusion, or GLI1 amplification usually with CDK4 and MDM2 co-amplification, rather than a MIR143-NOTCH fusion
Frequent S100 positivity and an inconsistent immunoprofile (CD56, SMA, pan-CK variably positive); glomus tumour is consistently actin-positive and S100-negative
High mitotic count and necrosis in a substantial minority, with lymphovascular invasion
Malignant behaviour is the rule rather than the rare exception it is in glomus tumour
assertion.notes: MONDO has no class for GLI1-altered / GLI1-amplified soft tissue tumour (a MONDO search for "GLI1" returns only the HGNC gene record), so this differential is deliberately recorded without a disease_term rather than mapped to an approximate parent.

selected_evidence.snippet: No consistent immunoprofile was detected, with positivity for CD56 (six cases), S100 (four cases), SMA (two cases), and pan-CK (one case).

assertion.name: Solitary fibrous tumour (formerly haemangiopericytoma)
assertion.description: Historically confused with glomus tumour because "haemangiopericytoma" was once used for any perivascular-patterned tumour. Solitary fibrous tumour is now defined by the NAB2-STAT6 fusion with nuclear STAT6 expression and CD34 positivity, and is a fibroblastic rather than pericytic lesion; the staghorn-vessel pattern it shares with glomus tumour is a non-specific architectural feature.
distinguishing_features: Patternless spindle-cell proliferation with ropey collagen and staghorn vessels, not uniform round perivascular glomus cells
Nuclear STAT6 (NAB2-STAT6 fusion) and CD34 positive; glomus tumour is STAT6/CD34 negative and SMA positive
Fibroblastic lineage, not pericytic; no NOTCH fusion
Typically a deep-seated or serosal mass, painless, without the cold-sensitivity triad
assertion.notes: Historically this differential carried no evidence item because no abstract in the reference set made the glomus-tumour-versus-SFT comparison directly. It is now backed from both sides: the NAB2-STAT6 / nuclear STAT6 discriminator by PMID:24030747, and the actin-plus-MIR143-NOTCH2 glomus-tumour signature by PMID:31189998, which lists solitary fibrous tumour and glomus tumour/myopericytoma on the same differential. A single paper making the head-to-head comparison still does not appear to exist.

selected_evidence.snippet: In conclusion, STAT6 is a highly sensitive and almost perfectly specific immunohistochemical marker for SFT and can be helpful to distinguish this tumor type from histologic mimics.

assertion.name: Eccrine spiradenoma
assertion.description: A benign sweat-gland adnexal neoplasm and one of the classic causes of a small, exquisitely painful dermal nodule. It sits alongside glomus tumour on the standard differential for a painful cutaneous or subungual nodule, but is an epithelial (basaloid) tumour rather than a perivascular myoid one.

Cytokeratin-positive and SMA-negative in the neoplastic cells, the inverse of the glomus tumour immunophenotype
No cold hypersensitivity or Hildreth response
More often trunk or proximal-extremity dermis than subungual

assertion.name: PUS3-related intellectual disability and microcephaly syndrome

term.label: severe growth deficiency-strabismus-extensive dermal melanocytosis-intellectual disability syndrome

assertion.description: The single most confusable entity. PUS3 (hgnc:25461) is another stand-alone pseudouridine synthase whose loss causes an autosomal recessive intellectual disability and microcephaly syndrome (MONDO:0014886, OMIM:617051, also known as MRT55). Both disorders are described in the literature as caused by "impaired pseudouridylation" and both were characterised by overlapping author groups, so gene-agnostic reading of that phrase will merge them.
distinguishing_features: Molecular: PUS3 (hgnc:25461) versus PUS7 (hgnc:26033). Different genes, different MONDO entities, different OMIM numbers (617051 versus 618342).

Substrate position: PUS3 isomerises uridine at tRNA positions 38 and 39, whereas PUS7 acts at position 13 (and at position 35 of pre-tRNA-Tyr). A tRNA modification assay therefore distinguishes them biochemically, and this is the cleanest functional discriminator.

Clinical: the PUS3 MONDO entity carries severe growth deficiency, strabismus and extensive dermal melanocytosis as label-level features. Dermal melanocytosis has never been reported in PUS7 deficiency, and the PUS7 behavioural signature of very-early-onset aggression is not part of the PUS3 label.

selected_evidence.snippet: Consistent with the known role of Pus3 in isomerizing uracil to pseudouridine at positions 38 and 39 in tRNA, we found a significant reduction in this post-transcriptional modification of tRNA in patient cells.

assertion.name: PUS1-related myopathy, lactic acidosis and sideroblastic anaemia (MLASA1)

term.label: myopathy, lactic acidosis, and sideroblastic anemia 1

assertion.description: The first pseudouridine synthase disease described in humans, caused by biallelic PUS1 variants (hgnc:15508). Despite sharing the "deficient pseudouridylation" mechanism language with PUS7 disease, the phenotype is almost disjoint: a mitochondrial oxidative-phosphorylation disorder restricted to skeletal muscle and bone marrow.
distinguishing_features: Molecular: PUS1 (hgnc:15508) versus PUS7 (hgnc:26033); MONDO:0024553 versus MONDO:0032687.

Compartment: PUS1 deficiency is proposed to act through deficient pseudouridylation of MITOCHONDRIAL tRNAs, whereas PUS7 acts on cytosolic tRNAs, mRNAs and tRNA-derived fragments. This is the mechanistic reason the two phenotypes barely overlap.

Clinical: MLASA1 presents with exercise intolerance, myopathy, lactic acidosis and sideroblastic anaemia. Intellectual disability, microcephaly and aggression are not part of it, and conversely myopathy, lactic acidosis and sideroblastic anaemia have never been reported in PUS7 deficiency. A patient with anaemia and a raised lactate is not a PUS7 candidate.

selected_evidence.snippet: Mitochondrial myopathy and sideroblastic anemia (MLASA) is a rare, autosomal recessive oxidative phosphorylation disorder specific to skeletal muscle and bone marrow.

assertion.name: Smith-Magenis syndrome
assertion.description: The closest non-genetic-family phenocopy on behavioural grounds. Smith-Magenis syndrome, caused by the recurrent 17p11.2 deletion or by intragenic RAI1 variants, combines intellectual disability, sleep disturbance, aggression, self-injurious behaviour, motor stereotypies and short stature. That is a near-complete overlap with the "less common but more peculiar" cluster that PMID:42226002 proposes as the discriminating signature of PUS7 deficiency, which means the very features that are supposed to raise suspicion of PUS7 disease also describe Smith-Magenis. This differential exists because the behavioural gestalt collides, not because the genes or mechanisms are related.
distinguishing_features: Molecular: a 17p11.2 microdeletion or heterozygous RAI1 variant, autosomal dominant and usually de novo, versus biallelic recessive PUS7. Chromosomal microarray detects the common deletion and will be normal in PUS7 disease.

Sleep: Smith-Magenis has a characteristic inverted circadian melatonin rhythm with the classic phenotype of daytime sleepiness and night waking. The sleep disturbance reported in PUS7 deficiency is a single-case observation with no described circadian signature.
Head size: progressive postnatal microcephaly is a core PUS7 feature and is not characteristic of Smith-Magenis, so serial head-circumference plotting is a cheap discriminator.
Visceral involvement: Smith-Magenis includes craniofacial, skeletal and visceral anomalies. PUS7 deficiency has mild non-specific facial dysmorphism and no visceral anomalies.

selected_evidence.snippet: Smith-Magenis syndrome (SMS) is a complex syndrome involving intellectual disabilities, sleep disturbance, behavioural problems, and a variety of craniofacial, skeletal, and visceral anomalies.

assertion.name: Other tRNA-modification intellectual disability syndromes
assertion.description: PUS7 disease sits inside a growing class of autosomal recessive intellectual disability syndromes caused by loss of a single tRNA modification, all of which share intellectual disability with variable microcephaly and short stature and are therefore clinically indistinguishable without sequencing. The record is bound to the ADAT3 entity (MONDO:0014119, adenosine-to-inosine editing at wobble position 34), which is the most common cause of autosomal recessive intellectual disability in Arabia and is therefore the highest-prior alternative in the very populations where PUS7 families have been ascertained.
distinguishing_features: Molecular: ADAT3 (hgnc:25151) wobble-position inosine editing, NSUN2 (hgnc:25994, MONDO:0012613) 5-methylcytosine, TRMT10A 1-methylguanosine at position 9, WDR4 7-methylguanosine at position 46, THUMPD1 tRNA acetylation. None of these is a pseudouridine synthase, and none produces a position-13 pseudouridine defect.
Assay: the discriminating test is which modification is missing. PUS7 disease shows loss of pseudouridine at tRNA position 13 with other pseudouridine positions in the same tRNAs intact.
Clinical: strabismus is a label-level feature of the ADAT3 entity and is not reported in PUS7 deficiency; conversely very-early-onset aggression is the PUS7 signature.
assertion.notes: One record is used for the class rather than one per gene, because the shared diagnostic logic (sequence the child; identify which tRNA modification is absent) is identical for all of them and duplicating it per gene would add length without adding discrimination. The bound term is the ADAT3 entity; NSUN2 disease is MONDO:0012613, and dismech already carries a separate entry for the THUMPD1-related disorder. The class-level point is supported by the quoted sentences, which name the class explicitly.

selected_evidence.snippet: For example, the most common form of autosomal recessive ID in Arabia was found to be due to mutation of ADAT3, which edits adenosine to inosine at the wobble position 34 of mature tRNA

assertion.name: PUS7L-related neurodevelopmental disorder
assertion.description: PUS7L (hgnc:25276) is the paralogue of PUS7 and is a separate gene. A patient with severe global developmental delay and epilepsy carrying a homozygous truncating PUS7L variant was noted in passing by the same group that characterised PUS7 disease. Because the gene symbols differ by a single trailing character, this is a high-risk symbol-level confusion, distinct from the mechanism-level confusion posed by PUS1 and PUS3.
distinguishing_features: Molecular: PUS7L is hgnc:25276, PUS7 is hgnc:26033. They are distinct paralogous genes at distinct loci, and PUS7L has its own tRNA targets, mapped in PMID:41136621.

Clinical: the reported PUS7L phenotype prominently included epilepsy, whereas PMID:30778726 positively asserts the LACK of epilepsy as a consistent feature of PUS7 deficiency. Seizures should therefore push a differential toward PUS7L, not PUS7.
assertion.notes: Deliberately left UNBOUND. `runoak -i sqlite:obo:mondo relationships --direction down HGNC:25276` returns no rows, and a MONDO label search for PUS7L returns nothing, so there is no MONDO disease term for a PUS7L-related disorder to bind to. Binding a generic neurodevelopmental-disorder term here would assert an entity that does not exist in the ontology. The gene identity is instead carried in the description and distinguishing features. When MONDO mints a PUS7L disease class this record should be bound.

selected_evidence.snippet: In addition, we recently encountered a patient with severe global developmental delay and epilepsy with a homozygous truncating variant in PUS7L (manuscript under review).

assertion.description: Not a phenotypic mimic so much as a documented co-occurring second diagnosis. assertion.name: ABCC8-related congenital hyperinsulinism
assertion.description: ABCC8 encodes SUR1, the pancreatic sulfonylurea receptor, and differs from ABCC9 by one character in the gene symbol and one paralogue in the same KATP family. Biallelic ABCC8 loss of function is the commonest genetic cause of congenital hyperinsulinism, which is a neonatal hypoglycaemia disorder with no myopathy and no primary white matter disease. The mechanistic parallel is real - both are recessive loss-of-function sulfonylurea-receptor channelopathies - which is exactly why the literature is easy to misattribute, and why every mechanistic sentence in this entry was checked for which receptor it names.
distinguishing_features: Caused by ABCC8 (SUR1), not ABCC9 (SUR2)
Presents with severe persistent neonatal hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia, which is not a feature of AIMS
Tissue of action is the pancreatic beta cell, not skeletal muscle, brain vasculature or myocardium
Focal and diffuse histological forms with 18F-DOPA PET localisation, a workup with no AIMS counterpart
Any brain injury is secondary to hypoglycaemia, whereas AIMS white matter disease is primary and present without hypoglycaemia

assertion.description: The other ABCC9 disease and the single most important entity to separate from AIMS. Cantu syndrome is caused by GAIN-of-function ABCC9 variants and is autosomal dominant, whereas AIMS is caused by biallelic LOSS-of-function variants and is autosomal recessive. The two are therefore allelic in the trivial sense of sharing a gene but are mechanistically opposite, and the Cantu literature is far larger, so a paper that says only "ABCC9 variant" without stating direction of effect cannot be used for either disease. Clinically Cantu is dominated by congenital hypertrichosis, coarse facial features, cardiomegaly with enhanced systolic function and osteochondrodysplasia, with intellect typically normal - none of which describes AIMS. Conversely no AIMS patient has had hypertrichosis, and AIMS cardiac disease is reduced rather than enhanced systolic function.

Autosomal dominant with de novo missense alleles clustering at Arg1154, not autosomal recessive truncating or splice alleles
Congenital hypertrichosis is characteristic; no AIMS patient has had hypertrichosis
Coarse facial features and osteochondrodysplasia, versus the distinct AIMS facies with prominent supraorbital ridges
Cardiomegaly with enhanced systolic function and patent ductus arteriosus, versus reduced systolic function in older AIMS patients
Intellect typically normal despite common developmental delay, versus intellectual disability in essentially all AIMS patients
Cerebral white matter hyperintensity resembling periventricular leukomalacia is an AIMS hallmark, not a Cantu feature
The Cantu GeneReviews "agents to avoid" list (minoxidil, diazoxide, ACE inhibitors) is specific to KATP overactivity and must not be transferred to AIMS

assertion.name: DEND syndrome
assertion.description: Developmental delay, epilepsy and neonatal diabetes - the KATP gain-of-function neurodevelopmental syndrome caused by activating variants in KCNJ11 or ABCC8. assertion.name: Heterozygous ABCC9 loss-of-function cardiac phenotypes
assertion.description: A cluster of monoallelic ABCC9 loss-of-function associations - dilated cardiomyopathy, Brugada and early repolarization syndromes, and idiopathic ventricular fibrillation - reported in adults with no intellectual disability, no myopathy and no white matter disease. These share both the gene and the direction of effect with AIMS, which makes them the subtlest confusion in the ABCC9 literature: a paper titled "loss-of-function ABCC9 variant" may be describing a heterozygous adult arrhythmia case, not AIMS. Zygosity is the discriminator. AIMS carriers in the published families have no conserved clinical pathology.
distinguishing_features: Monoallelic (heterozygous) ABCC9 loss of function, versus the biallelic state required for AIMS
Isolated cardiac presentation in adults - arrhythmia or cardiomyopathy - without intellectual disability, myopathy or white matter disease
AIMS heterozygous parents show no conserved clinical pathology, so these associations are not simply the AIMS carrier state
Some of the reported alleles sit in the SUR2A-specific exon, a cardiac-restricted isoform region
assertion.notes: Deliberately left unbound. There is no single MONDO term for "heterozygous ABCC9 loss-of-function cardiac phenotype": the reported associations span dilated cardiomyopathy, Brugada syndrome, early repolarization syndrome and idiopathic ventricular fibrillation, and binding any one of those general disease terms would misrepresent the group and would also bind a term whose gene attribution is not ABCC9-specific. The dismech entries Dilated_Cardiomyopathy and Familial_Atrial_Fibrillation already carry the ABCC9 heterozygous-cardiac material in their own gene sections; this differential exists to keep that literature out of the AIMS phenotype set, not to duplicate it.

selected_evidence.snippet: The female proband presented with several episodes of ventricular fibrillation and hypokalemia upon emotional stress.

selected_evidence.snippet: Two serum samples from one patient showed neutralizing antibodies against TBE virus.

assertion.name: Cellulitis
assertion.description: Bacterial skin infection that can mimic early erythema migrans.
distinguishing_features: Painful, warm, expanding erythema often with fever.
No central clearing.
Responds rapidly to anti-staphylococcal/streptococcal therapy.

selected_evidence.snippet: atypical vesicular features... resulted in multiple misdiagnoses and delayed treatment

assertion.name: Multiple Sclerosis and Other Demyelinating Myelopathies
assertion.description: Demyelinating CNS disease that can mimic neuroborreliosis with cord lesions.
distinguishing_features: Oligoclonal bands without intrathecal Borrelia antibodies.
Typical MS lesion distribution.
Relapsing course without tick exposure.

selected_evidence.snippet: Examples... newly diagnosed included multiple sclerosis

assertion.description: Lone star tick-associated erythema migrans–like rash without Borrelia burgdorferi infection.
distinguishing_features: Occurs after Amblyomma americanum bite in southeastern/south-central US; Borrelia testing negative.
Typically lacks systemic neurologic or cardiac involvement seen in disseminated Lyme.

selected_evidence.snippet: southern tick-associated rash illness (STARI)

assertion.name: Rheumatoid Arthritis
assertion.description: Chronic symmetric inflammatory polyarthritis.
distinguishing_features: Small-joint symmetric involvement with RF/anti-CCP positivity.
No tick exposure history or erythema migrans.
Nodules and erosions on imaging.

distinguishing_features: Elevated cardiac biomarkers and viral serologies.
Absence of erythema migrans or Lyme serology.
Persistent AV block without rapid reversal on antibiotics.

selected_evidence.snippet: Comprehensive investigations excluded other bradyarrhythmia causes, such as Lyme disease, sarcoidosis, and myocarditis

assertion.description: Acute bacterial arthritis of large joints.
distinguishing_features: Very high synovial WBC with positive Gram stain/culture.
Lacks migratory arthralgias and Borrelia serology.
Requires urgent drainage.

assertion.name: Non-24-Hour Sleep-Wake Rhythm Disorder
assertion.description: A circadian disorder in which the clock fails to entrain to the 24-hour day at all, so sleep timing drifts progressively later (or, rarely, earlier) day after day. Most common in totally blind individuals lacking photic input.
distinguishing_features: Sleep timing progressively drifts rather than being stably advanced
Symptoms cycle between asymptomatic and symptomatic periods as the endogenous rhythm moves in and out of alignment
Actigraphy over several weeks shows a characteristic staircase pattern rather than a fixed early schedule
Strongly associated with total blindness and absent photic input

selected_evidence.snippet: strategically timed melatonin (for the treatment of DSWPD, blind adults with N24SWD, and children/ adolescents with ISWRD and comorbid neurological disorders)

assertion.name: Shift Work Disorder
assertion.description: An extrinsic circadian disorder in which the misalignment is imposed by an externally mandated schedule rather than arising from the endogenous clock. Included because it is the standard exclusion when a patient reports sleep at unconventional hours, and because shift work and transmeridian travel were exclusion criteria in the major ASPS observational protocols.

disease_term.preferred_term: circadian rhythm sleep disorder, shift work type

term.label: circadian rhythm sleep disorder, shift work type

distinguishing_features: Caused by external behavioral/occupational factors rather than an intrinsic clock abnormality
Resolves or substantially improves when the imposed schedule is removed, whereas ASPS persists
Sleep timing follows the work roster rather than a stable early endogenous phase

selected_evidence.snippet: extrinsic circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorders, in which sleep disorders, such as jet lag or shift-work disorder, result from environmental changes that cause a mismatch between sleep-wakefulness times and internal circadian rhythms

assertion.name: Irregular Sleep-Wake Rhythm Disorder
assertion.description: Particularly relevant to the sporadic/age-related arm, since it arises in the same population - older adults, and especially those with dementia, in whom SCN degeneration is advanced. Whereas ASPS represents a coherent circadian rhythm shifted early, ISWRD represents loss of a consolidated rhythm altogether, with sleep fragmented into multiple bouts across the 24 hours. Sundowning and fragmented nocturnal sleep in dementia typically belong here rather than to ASPS.

disease_term.preferred_term: circadian rhythm sleep disorder, irregular sleep wake type

term.label: circadian rhythm sleep disorder, irregular sleep wake type

distinguishing_features: At least three irregular sleep episodes per 24-hour period, rather than one consolidated but early sleep episode
No stable phase relationship to clock time, so actigraphy shows fragmentation rather than a consistent early schedule
Total sleep across 24 hours may be normal but is not consolidated, whereas ASPS sleep is consolidated and normal in architecture
AASM gives it different treatment recommendations from ASWPD (melatonin in children/adolescents with comorbid neurological disorders; light therapy in elderly with dementia)

selected_evidence.snippet: Recommendations against the use of melatonin and discrete sleep-promoting medications are provided for demented elderly patients

assertion.name: Major Depressive Disorder with Early-Morning Awakening
assertion.description: A clinically important differential in the opposite direction - terminal insomnia is a classic melancholic feature of major depression, and an ASPS patient reporting that they always wake at 4 a.m. is readily misread as depressed. Conversely, a depressed patient may be misclassified as having a circadian disorder. Getting this wrong matters because the treatments diverge completely, and because PER3-associated FASP is itself reported alongside elevated depression and seasonality scores, so the two can genuinely co-occur.
distinguishing_features: Evening sleepiness is absent in depression; sleep onset is often delayed or unimpaired rather than involuntarily early
Sleep is nonrestorative in depression, whereas in ASPS it is restorative when taken at the preferred early hours
The whole circadian ensemble need not be phase-advanced in depression; DLMO is typically normal
Core depressive symptoms (anhedonia, low mood, guilt, appetite and psychomotor change) are present in depression and typically absent in ASPS

selected_evidence.snippet: We identified two rare variants in the circadian clock gene PERIOD3 (PER3-P415A/H417R) in humans with familial advanced sleep phase accompanied by higher Beck Depression Inventory and seasonality scores.

assertion.name: Obstructive Sleep Apnea Syndrome
assertion.description: Not a mimic so much as a confounder and frequent companion. Familial advanced sleep phase is most often discovered incidentally during evaluation for obstructive sleep apnea, and OSA independently causes fragmented sleep and daytime sleepiness that can obscure or be attributed to the circadian abnormality.
distinguishing_features: OSA produces snoring, witnessed apneas, and sleep fragmentation with non-restorative sleep at any schedule
OSA is confirmed by polysomnography and does not shift circadian phase markers
The two frequently coexist, so identifying OSA does not exclude ASPS

selected_evidence.snippet: is mostly discovered coincidentally in the presence of other sleep disorders, mainly obstructive sleep apnea syndrome (OSAS)

assertion.name: Insomnia Disorder
assertion.description: Chronic insomnia is the most frequent misdiagnosis in ASPS, because the early-morning awakening is reported as terminal insomnia. This misclassification commonly leads to hypnotic prescription, which suppresses the symptom without correcting circadian phase and carries particular risk (falls, confusion, next-day impairment) in the older adults in whom advanced phase is most prevalent.
distinguishing_features: In insomnia disorder sleep is poor regardless of when it is attempted; in ASPS sleep is normal once permitted at the advanced biological time
Sleep-onset latency is prolonged even at the preferred bedtime in insomnia disorder, but short in ASPS
A sleep diary showing consistently early, consolidated, restorative sleep on free days discriminates the two

selected_evidence.snippet: CRSWDs are easily mistaken for insomnia or early waking up, resulting in inappropriate treatment.

assertion.name: Delayed Sleep-Wake Phase Disorder
assertion.description: The mirror-image intrinsic circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorder, and by far the more commonly diagnosed of the two. Both are disorders of sleep timing with normal sleep when the preferred schedule is followed, and they share almost all of their clinical vocabulary - which is precisely why the literatures are easy to conflate. The direction of the phase shift is opposite and so is the treatment: DSWPD is treated with morning light and evening melatonin to advance the clock, ASPS with evening light to delay it. Applying DSWPD treatment to ASPS would worsen it.

disease_term.preferred_term: circadian rhythm sleep disorder, delayed sleep phase type

term.label: circadian rhythm sleep disorder, delayed sleep phase type

distinguishing_features: Sleep onset and offset are late (typically 02:00-06:00 onset) rather than early
Presenting complaint is sleep-onset insomnia and difficulty awakening in the morning, rather than evening sleepiness and early-morning awakening
Dim light melatonin onset (DLMO) is late rather than early
Onset is predominantly in adolescence rather than in early adulthood or with aging
Treatment direction is opposite - morning light and evening melatonin, versus evening light for ASPS

selected_evidence.snippet: strategically timed melatonin (for the treatment of DSWPD, blind adults with N24SWD, and children/ adolescents with ISWRD and comorbid neurological disorders), and light therapy with or without accompanying behavioral interventions (adults with ASWPD, children/adolescents with DSWPD, and elderly with dementia)
